name: Medical Exam Gloves
description: Size the market for disposable medical exam gloves.
formula: TAM = Population x Penetration_rate x Purchase_frequency x Average_spend
solution_logic: Step 1: Identify addressable population = target_population x addressable_segment
Step 2: Apply penetration rate = addressable_population x penetration_rate
Step 3: Calculate annual spend per user = purchase_frequency x avg_spend_per_purchase
Step 4: Calculate TAM = penetrating_users x annual_spend_per_user
key_insight: Market sizing is about defensible assumptions, not precision. Show your logic clearly -- the interviewer is testing your structure, not your arithmetic.
common_mistakes: Sizing the total population instead of the addressable segment
Forgetting purchase frequency -- confusing annual vs per-transaction spend
Not sanity-checking the output against known benchmarks
framework_soundbite: Top-down or bottom-up -- pick one, state your assumptions, and sanity-check the output. The logic matters more than the number.
business_contexts: a medical supply manufacturer evaluating a new glove production line
a hospital procurement group sizing annual glove demand
question_patterns: A medical supply manufacturer is deciding whether to add a new glove production line and wants to size annual demand from hospitals and clinics.

prompts.beginner: Estimate the total addressable market for disposable medical exam gloves.
prompts.intermediate: A medical supply manufacturer is deciding whether to add a new glove production line and wants to size annual demand from hospitals and clinics.
prompts.advanced: A contract manufacturer is being asked to commit capital to a new glove production line based on a distributor's demand forecast that leadership suspects is optimistic. Build an independent view of the addressable market before approving the capex.
